segments.text: Seventeen days. That's how long a rough diamond packet takes to reach dispatch in this factory... yet people work on it for only a few hours. So where does all that time go? And what if you could go back to last week... and change one decision? Meet RealityCheck: a time machine for the factory floor.

It's a Frankenstein. Five parts that were never meant to share a body. A history that can never change the past. A simulation engine that never guesses. Patterns from a real factory's month of data. An AI analyst that is forbidden to calculate. And one app, where every number tells you exactly where it came from.

Start with what really happened. Packets spend a huge share of their lives... parked in the rough store. On the workflow, these are the haunted stages: where packets lose the most time, with nobody working on them. And the worst one? Parking.

Now, let's go back in time. A scenario forks from a recorded moment... and changes just one decision. In this one, we halve the time packets sit parked. In this one, we hire three more inspectors instead. Then the engine replays the factory, from that moment forward, under each decision.

And the result? Halving parking finishes the work about thirty percent sooner... and on-time delivery jumps from fifty-seven to sixty-two percent. Each solid dot is when an order really finishes. Its ghost... is when it would have finished. And where history already knows, a diamond shows what truly happened.
And three more inspectors? Completion doesn't move. Not by a minute. Cost goes up nine percent. More people only help where a stage is actually waiting for capacity.

Claude explains the result, but only from stored evidence, and every number it writes is checked against the simulation. Look closely: it says the evidence does not isolate a cause. It refuses to invent one. And if it ever states a number the results can't support, the built-in analyst steps in instead.

But can you trust the engine? A backtest simulates past dates, changing nothing, and compares the result with what was recorded. On one real factory, imported privately, it's within about a fifth on packets finished... and we publish exactly where it's wrong.
Built spec-first with Kiro: steering rules, eleven specs, and hooks. And for Kiroween, a night theme, with exactly the same contrast. RealityCheck. See the future... before you change the present.
